subject: Syntech data retention temporal carveout — pilot proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@syntech.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@syntech.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes — Syntech data handling needs

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo today — Luca and I appreciated how Redwood routes and the caching controls. To summarize our top requirements so we don't miss anything:

- Data residency: All inference requests for our EU tenant must stay in the Frankfurt region
- PII/PHI: We need an option where user utterances containing PHI are not retained at all (0-retention) and are also excluded from any debugging logs or trace dumps
- Shortened logs: For non-PII usage we'd accept a shortened log window (14 days) for troubleshooting only
- Embeddings: We need clarification on whether embeddings are stored and for how long; if stored, they must be zero-retention or customer-managed
- Auditability: We need access to request-level audit logs (redacted as needed) and an exportable chain of custody for a 30-day period during the pilot
- Keys: KMS integration and customer-managed keys are mandatory

Could you sketch a concrete carveout schedule and what it would mean for SLAs/latency/cost? We're evaluating two procurement paths: a standard Dedicated deployment vs a Private VPC — both would need the same retention guarantees. Also, can you share SOC2 artifacts and the kinds of evidence we can get for the pilot?

Next steps from our side: Luca will prepare a security questionnaire and contracts@ will share a draft SOW.

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Product Security — Syntech AI

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 09:00 Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the time today!
>
> — Priya
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@syntech.ai>, Luca Moretti <luca.moretti@syntech.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, contracts@syntech.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Syntech data retention temporal carveout — draft options

Maria / Luca —

Appreciate the clear list. I put together three practical options and a suggested pilot path so you can weigh risk vs. unit cost. I'm attaching a short PDF and an XLSX with cost modeling; below is a concise summary.

Option A — Strict 0-retention endpoint (per-call redaction):
- All request/response payloads that match your PHI rules are dropped immediately after response generation; no KV cache entries are persisted
- No debugging traces retained; request-level audit records are written only as a hashed token (no PII) for 30 days
- Estimated cost impact: +18% per-token due to disabled caching and extra redaction passes

Option B — Hybrid shortlog window (PII removed on ingest):
- Non-PII traffic: retained for 14 days for debugging; PII fields are redacted at ingress and kept only in ephemeral memory
- Embeddings: treated as sensitive; default is 0-retention unless explicitly allowed and encrypted to a customer KMS
- Cost impact: +6% per-token; small latency bump for on-the-fly redaction

Option C — Private deployment with tenant-enforced retention policies:
- Customer-managed control plane (VPC); retention policies enforced per-tenant with audit hooks
- Best for strict compliance but higher TCO and longer onboarding

Pilot proposal (recommended):
1) Start with Option B for 30 days on a canary subset (EU tenant routed to Frankfurt).
2) Simultaneously run 10% of sensitive flows through Option A
3) Collect three metrics: 99th pct latency, error-rate increase, and incident debug lead time

Artifacts we can supply this week:
- SOC2 summary (attached)
- Example redaction ruleset and the proposed carveout schedule (attached)
- A draft SOW/DocuSign link once we align on scope

Questions we have for you:
- Do you have a canonical PHI field list we should use as a baseline for the redaction rules?
- Would Syntech be open to a short engineering spike (2 days) to confirm embedding behavior under Option B?

Looping in Marissa (contracts) and Soojin (privacy) for redlines and evidence packs. I’ll put a timeline suggestion below.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: syntech-carveout-proposal-v1.pdf, redaction-pilot-plan.xlsx, SOC2-summary-2026.pdf
From: Luca Moretti <luca.moretti@syntech.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@syntech.ai>, contracts@syntech.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:47:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Syntech data retention temporal carveout — follow-ups

Priya —

Thanks for the clear options. A few clarifications from our security team:

- PHI definition: we will send a canonical field list tomorrow, but from now assume names, national IDs, clinical notes, and any free-text flagged by our regex engines are PHI
- Embeddings: if they're required to be 0-retention we need assurance they will not be used for model re-training and that any cached vectors are truncated/zeroed immediately
- Per-tenant enforcement: critical — we cannot have cross-tenant caching or global caches that could leak between tenants
- Contract ask: we want retention language to be explicit in the MSA and a narrow carveout addendum for the pilot (SOW)

Luca

On Wed, Dec 2, 2026 at 08:22 Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Understood — we will ensure per-tenant cache isolation and a dedicated Frankfurt routing policy for the pilot.
>
> — Priya
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Syntech data retention temporal carveout — pilot proposal and next steps

Maria / Luca — quick update and concrete next steps so we can get you an SOW before EoWeek: 

1) Marissa (contracts) will draft a pilot addendum with explicit retention clauses (we'll include Option B as default with an Option A path) — expected by Tue 08 Dec
2) Soojin (privacy) will prepare a one-page evidence pack (redaction design + proof points from prior pilots) and confirm the SOC2 artifacts we can share — expected tomorrow
3) Engineering spike: we propose a 2-day spike next week to validate embedding zero-retention semantics and tenant cache isolation. We'd need a small set of representative payloads (anonymized) and a point of contact — can Luca/your infra team share a Slack handle?
4) DocuSign/SOW: once Marissa has the addendum draft we'll push a DocuSign link to contracts@syntech.ai. We estimate the pilot kickoff 10 business days after signed SOW.

Quick asks from us: please send the canonical PHI field list and confirm whether Syntech prefers KMS with AWS KMS keys or a short-term BYOK HSM for the pilot. Also confirm your preferred latency SLO (we'll size canary throughput accordingly).

If useful, I can do a short call with your security team on Tuesday to walk the proposed audit logs and hashed-record approach.

Thanks — looping Marissa and Soojin here to pick up legal/privacy items.

Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0133

Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>: will draft addendum
